finding: NO_RAW_HEX_COLOR treated the Seed color's one unavoidable literal hex as an exception recognized only via a self-reported code comment, which could just as easily be used to hide a real violation.
change: Moved the Seed exception to a structurally-recognized <html data-seed="#xxxxxx"> attribute; scripts/design-lint.mjs now exempts only that exact attribute value, not comments. All 5 example screens migrated to the new pattern.

finding: buildSemantics() only computed an onColor()-derived foreground for primary (primary-foreground). Every other role (secondary/accent/success/warning/danger/info) and the chart-1..6 palette had no equivalent, so button/icon text on those solid backgrounds fell back to hardcoded #fff/#000 in both the production docs site and freshly generated example screens.
change: Generalized buildSemantics() to compute an -on-solid token for all 6 non-primary roles across light/dark/hc, and added chartForegrounds() for the chart palette. Added contrast-based unit tests for both. Updated the 5 example screens to use the new tokens instead of hardcoded exceptions.

finding: SHADOW_ONLY_ON_FLOATING_LAYER was automationStatus:"manual" and, as literally written ("Card/Panel = never, no exceptions"), didn't distinguish layer-level containers from small interactive controls (Button/Input/Slider already ship shadow-xs). Researched Atlassian/Material/Carbon elevation guidance: the real distinguishing factor is shadow strength + whether the element structurally floats, not component type.
change: Refined the rule: shadow-xs exempt everywhere; shadow-sm+ requires position:fixed/absolute or a floating-UI selector keyword. Implemented as a static CSS-rule-block detector. Running it against index.html found 4 real pre-existing violations (.cardc.hover, .comp-tile:hover, .tpl-frame, .promptbox) that had shipped despite the (previously unenforced) elevation doc prohibiting them; all fixed to rely on border/background only.

finding: ACCENT_BRAND_MARK_ONLY, FOCUS_VISIBLE_REQUIRED, and CONTRAST_AA_MINIMUM were the last 3 of 8 rules still automationStatus:"manual" (unchecked except by eye).
change: Automated all three: accent via the same selector-keyword CSS-rule-block scan as the shadow detector; focus-visible via a file-level outline:none / :focus-visible pairing check; contrast by actually calling buildPalettes/buildSemantics/contrast from src/color-engine.js (via createRequire) across all 7 SEED_PRESETS x light/dark/hc for any CSS rule setting both a semantic background and color token directly.

finding: The new CONTRAST_AA_MINIMUM detector immediately found a real, previously-unnoticed accessibility bug: .gallery-main and th both paired foreground-subtle on surface-muted, landing at ~3.9:1 across all 7 seed presets — under the 4.5:1 AA floor. Neither a human reviewer nor the AI had caught this by eye across even one of the two screens.
change: Both switched to foreground-muted on the same background (~5.7:1, comfortably AA). No rule/token change needed here — this was a token *usage* mistake in generated UI, not a gap in the token set itself.
